in_hebrew.name: נתנאל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: נתנאל הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'מתנת אלוהים' או 'אלוהים נתן'. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'נתן' שפירושו 'לתת' ו'אל' שפירושו 'אלוהים'. השם נתנאל מוזכר בתנ'ך כבן של קלובי, איש ממשפחת יהודה.

in_greek.name: Ναθαναήλ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Ναθαναήλ είναι ελληνικό όνομα που σημαίνει 'Θεός έδωκεν' ή 'Το δώρο του Θεού'. Το όνομα προέρχεται από τις εβραϊκές λέξεις 'נatan' που σημαίνει 'να δώσω' και 'אל' που σημαίνει 'Θεός'. Στο Ευαγγέλιο του Ιωάννη, ο Ναθαναήλ ήταν ένας από τους μαθητές του Ιησού.

in_latin.name: Natanael
in_latin.long_meaning: Natanael est nomen Latinum quod significat 'Deus donavit' vel 'Donum Dei'. Nomen derivatur ex radicibus Hebraeis 'נatan' quod significat 'donare' et 'אל' quod significat 'Deus'. In traditione Christiana, Natanael fuit unus de discipulis Iesu Christi.

in_english.name: Natanael
in_english.meaning: Gift of God or God has given
in_english.long_meaning: Natanael is a Christian name that originated from the Hebrew name 'נתנאל' (Natan-El), meaning 'gift of God' or 'God has given'. The name is composed of two Hebrew words: 'natan', meaning 'to give', and 'El', meaning 'God'. In the New Testament, Nathanael (Natanael) was one of Jesus' twelve apostles, also known as Bartholomew. The name has been used in various Christian cultures and is associated with spiritual significance, humility, and devotion.

data.cultural_impact: The name Natanael holds a unique and interesting cultural significance in Christianity. It was the name given to one of the twelve apostles, Saint Matthew records in the New Testament of the Bible (Matthew 11:29). Natanael is often associated with a prominent early Christian hymn called the "Bethlehem Star Carol," which includes the line, "Natanael, and Bethlehem's King, Were the first to see Thee lie, in the Lord's manger, At whose voice the angels sung." This hymn highlights Natanael's role as a witness to the birth of Jesus and underscores his faith and devotion.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Natanael has a profound spiritual significance, reflecting the humility and devotion of one who recognizes God's hand in his life. In Hebrew, Natanael means "God has given" or "God has sent." Thisname serves as a reminder that every person is a gift from God, and each one has a unique spiritual purpose. In the biblical account, Natanael encounters Jesus and, despite initially expressing skepticism, is given a vision of Christ's heavenly origin. After this powerful spiritual experience, Natanael declares, "You are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel." (John 1:49). This encounter teaches us that even the most ordinary encounters can reveal God's divine presence in our lives. The name Natanael thus signifies the blessings and grace that come from God's intervention and the importance of remaining faithful and open to His will in our lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Natanael, meaning "given by God," symbolizes faith and divine guidance. It underlines the belief that one's true identity and purpose are bestowed by the divine, encouraging trust in God's plan.

biblical_reference.note: Nathanael was one of Jesus' twelve apostles, introduced by Philip.

historical_references.reference: Nathanael of Cappadocia, a famous ascetic and hermit, is mentioned in the works of Saint Basil the Great and Saint Gregory of Nyssa.

modern_usage.modern_context: Natanael is a name of Hebrew origin, meaning 'given by God'. In the Christian tradition, it is associated with the figure of Nathanael of Cappadocia, a famous ascetic and hermit. Today, Natanael is used as a given name and can be found in various records and databases, including social media and genealogy websites.
